en: O Lord of the World, whose incomparable dark body is perpetually reddened by the saffron from the nipples of Kamalā’s breasts;
O Lord of the Venkata mountain, whose eyes are as long as lotuses—may you be victorious! 1.

O Lord of the Bull-Mountain, jewel upon the crowns of all deities headed by the Four-faced, Six-faced, and Five-faced ones; O you who are compassionate toward those who seek refuge, O treasure-house of essence, protect me! 2.

O Hari, Lord of the Bull-Mountain, quickly protect me with supreme compassion, for I am filled with hundreds of offenses committed at every moment, which are exceedingly unbearable due to their extreme frequency. 3.

O noble-minded one, I consider none higher than the Beloved of Kamalā, who delights in giving abundantly what is desired by the people on Mount Veṅkaṭa, and who is described by the Vedas as the Supreme Deity. 4.

I consider nothing superior to the son of Vasudeva, who is surrounded by hundreds of millions of cowherd women overcome by the sound of his flute, who is equal to ten million Cupids, who is cherished like a fresh sprout, and who bestows happiness. 5.
O mine of delightful qualities, son of Daśaratha, sole wielder of the bow for the world, O one of steadfast intellect!
O Leader of the Raghus, Rāma, Lord of Lakṣmī, All-pervading One, grantor of boons, O God, ocean of compassion, be gracious! (6)

I bow to that great Raghu-Rāma, whose hands are as desirable as the daughter of the Earth (Sītā), whose lotus-face is as beautiful as the moon, and who is the sun to the darkness that is the king of the night-stalkers (Rāvaṇa). 7.

Having abandoned the scion of the Raghus— who possesses a gracious countenance, is a true friend, is easily accessible, bestows happiness, is his own younger brother, has a beautiful form, and whose arrows are never in vain— I shall never, under any circumstances, worship anyone else at any time.
Without Veṅkaṭeśa there is no protector, no protector; I remember, I remember Veṅkaṭeśa always!
O Hare Veṅkaṭeśa! Be gracious, be gracious; O beloved Veṅkaṭeśa, grant me what is dear, grant it! 9.

O Lord Veṅkaṭeśa, having come from afar with the desire to prostrate at Your pair of lotus feet, I perform service; grant, grant me the fruit of eternal service through this single act of service! 10.
O Hari, O crest-jewel of the Śeṣa mountain, forgive, forgive me—the ignorant one—for all the faults I have committed. (11)
Thus ends the Śrī Veṅkaṭeśa Stotra.
